docs.title: MIND Documentation Hub
docs.text:
MIND is a simple self hosted reminder application that can send push notifications to your device. Set the reminder and forget about it!

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text:
The admin panel allows you to manage your MIND instance. It has multiple features regarding the management of your instance and its users. You can change how users authenticate and create accounts, download the logs, change the hosting settings, add/edit/delete users, export and import the database and restart or shutdown the application.

The settings for authentication, hosting, logging and database backups are all described on the 'Admin Settings' page.

Restrict Access

The panel gives you a lot of power, so it's important that nobody can access it but you (by changing the default password).

docs.title: Accessing the panel
docs.text: You can access the admin panel by logging into the admin account. The default username is admin and the default password is admin. How to change the password (which is strongly recommended) is described in the 'User Management' section.

docs.title: User Management
docs.text:
The admin panel allows you to manage the users on your instance. You can add new users, change the password of existing users and delete users. The ability to add users will always be there, regardless of the value of the 'Allow New Accounts' setting. If that setting is disabled (disallowing users to create accounts themselves), then the admin panel is the only place where new accounts can be made.

Click the large plus button to start adding an account. Enter a unique username and a password for the account, then click 'Add'. Click on the pen icon next to a user entry to change the username or password of the user. This is useful if the user has forgotten their password. You can also change the password of the admin user this way, which is strongly recommended. Use the bin icon to delete the user. You cannot delete the admin. Edit the admin account to not only change the password, but to also optionally setup MFA. The Apprise URL that you enter will be used to send the MFA code when trying to log into the account. The users can set the MFA code themselves in their account settings.

docs.title: Database
docs.text:
The 'Download Database' button allows you to download the complete MIND database. This file contains everything: all user accounts, their settings, notification services and reminders, and admin settings (authentication, hosting, etc.). This file represents a complete back-up of your MIND instance.

The admin panel offers the option to upload a database file to apply. There are multiple scenarios where you'd want to upload a database (import a backup):

  1. You can recover all data up to the point of database export in the case that something goes wrong.
  2. You can revert back to a stable state when trying something.
  3. You're moving to a new computer/instance and want to move all user data too.

Select the database file that you want to import for the 'Database File' input. Enabling the 'Keep Hosting Settings' option will copy the hosting settings from the current database over to the imported database. This will result in the instance being hosted with the same settings as it is now. If you leave this setting disabled, the hosting settings from the imported database will be used. That could result in the web-UI being hosted with different settings, potentially making it unreachable.

The uploaded file could be denied for multiple reasons:

  1. It is not an (sqlite) database file. Only import database files that you downloaded with the 'Download Database' button.
  2. The database file is too old. If the database is for such an old version of MIND, it could fail to migrate it.
  3. The database file is too new. If the database is for a newer version of MIND than the version that you upload it to, it's denied.

After importing the database, MIND will restart with the new database in use. It is required to log into the admin panel within 60 seconds in order to keep the newly imported database file. If you do not, the import will be reverted, MIND will restart again but now with the old database again. This is in order to protect you from breaking MIND if the database file is invalid or if the hosting settings make the UI unreachable (if you have the 'Keep Hosting Settings' option disabled).

The download button next to each database backup entry will download the backup file to your computer. The upload button next to each database backup entry will allow you to import/upload the backup, similar to uploading a database file yourself.

docs.title: Apprise Plugins
docs.text: If you have a custom Apprise plugin, then you click the 'Manage Paths' button to open a window where you can add the path to the file that the plugin is defined in. It will then become available to use inside MIND.

docs.title: Power
docs.text: You can use these buttons to restart or shutdown the application.

docs.title: How To Use
docs.text: This is a guide to using MIND, after installation and setup.

docs.title: Creating an account
docs.text: If you don't have an account yet, you can create one on the login page. Click on Or create an account to start creating one. If you do not see that option, then the administrator disabled registration. Only the administration can make an account for you then.

docs.title: Adding a notification service
docs.text:
A notification service is a way of sending a notification. For example an e-mail to a group of people or a PushBullet notification to a specific device. What the actual content of the notification is, is decided by the title and text of the reminder. The notification service only specifies in which way the title and text is sent. You set it up once, and then you can select it when creating a reminder. You can select one or more notification services for each reminder.

Go to the "Notification Services" tab in the web-UI and click the + button. Choose a platform, enter the required information and give the service a name. From then on, you can select the notification service when creating/editing a reminder.

docs.title: Adding a reminder
docs.text: There are two types of reminders: time dependent reminders ('normal reminders') and time independent reminders ('static reminders'). Then there are also 'templates', which you can use to create normal and static reminders faster.

docs.title: Normal Reminders
docs.text:
Normal reminders require a time that they need to be triggered on. By default, normal reminders are 'single-use' and disappear after they are triggered. However, it's also possible to have reminders repeat.

One of the ways a reminder can repeat is based on an interval like every 5 days or once per year. The first time the reminder will be sent is on the set time. The interval will then be added and the resulting time will be the next time the reminder will be triggered. Instead of repeating based on a certain time interval, it is also possible to repeat based on the week days. For example, if you select 'Mo' and 'Thu', the reminder will be triggered every Monday and Thursday. The time is based on the time set. The date of the time set decides when the reminder starts repeating. Lastly, you can supply your own Cron schedule that the reminder should follow.

In the UI, select the tab 'Reminders' and click the '+' button to add a new reminder.

  1. You can select a template to build upon. More info on that in the 'Templates' section.
  2. Select whether the reminder should be enabled. If the reminder is disabled, it will not be triggered.
  3. Select a colour that the reminder should have.
  4. Then use the dropdown to select whether the reminder is single-use or whether it should repeat. Then fill in the fields below it, based on what option you chose, to specify when and how often the reminder should trigger.
  5. At the bottom, select which notification service(s) should be used when sending the reminder.
  6. At the right side, give a title for the reminder and optionally a body/text.
  7. Clicking the 'Test' button will send the reminder, so that you can check if it works as desired. Then click 'Add' to finalise the creation.

Once it's added, the timer is set! When the set time is reached, the reminder will be sent.

docs.title: Static Reminders
docs.text:
Static reminders work the same way as normal reminders, except that there is no time aspect. There is no date, time or repetition. This is because static reminders are only triggered manually. Simply click on the reminder in the library and click the 'Trigger' button to send the reminder.

The use of this is to notify people on command. For example, a notification to your kids that you'll be late. You don't want to send such a thing on a certain time or interval, but instead on command. Or an e-mail to your team notifying them of a emergency meeting. With static reminders, you can set it up once and when needed click one button to notify everyone within seconds.

docs.title: Templates
docs.text: Templates can be used to make it easier to create (static) reminders by filling in fields when selecting it. In the UI, select the 'Templates' tab and click the '+' button to add a template. Templates can store the colour, title, notification service selection and body/text of the reminder. When saved, you can start using it in the creation of reminders. Simply select the template from the list and all the fields will be filled automatically. The only fields left are the time fields for normal reminders.

docs.title: Repeating Reminders at an Interval
docs.text:
It is possible to create a repeated reminder that triggers on a day that doesn't always exist. For example, a reminder that runs on leap day, every year. Or a reminder that runs on the 31st of the month, every month. The targeted days don't always exist when the reminder runs. MIND will run the reminder on a day that does exist, and comes before the targeted day. So for example, with the leap year example, that'd mean the reminder would run on the following days (D-M-Y format):

  • 29-2-2024
  • 28-2-2025
  • 28-2-2026
  • 28-2-2027
  • 29-2-2028

docs.title: Detecting Timezone Changes
docs.text:
MIND has handling for when the timezone of the computer that it runs on changes. It could for example be that the timezone switches between daylight savings time and standard time or that the computer is moved to another country where the timezone is different. If MIND detects this, the reminders are appropriately altered so that they still trigger at the same time. That means that if the reminder originally ran at 3 o'clock in the afternoon, then after the timezone switch the reminder will still run at 3 o'clock in the afternoon even though this is technically a different point in the absolute timeline.

It can take up to a day before MIND detects that the timezone has changed. On Windows it might require a restart of MIND before the change is detected.

docs.title: Docker
docs.text: On this page, you can find instructions on how to install MIND using Docker and how to update a Docker installation.

docs.title: Time settings
docs.text: Make sure to set all time related settings (time, date, timezone, etc.) correct on your computer, as MIND depends on it to work correctly.

docs.title: Install Docker
docs.text:
The first step is to install Docker if you don't have it installed already. The official Docker documentation hub offers great instructions on how to install docker CLI and Docker Desktop. Take notice of whether you installed the 'Docker CLI' (the Docker documentation also calls this 'Docker CE') or 'Docker Desktop', for future instructions.

Quick introduction to Docker

Docker allows you to create little virtual computers, called 'containers'. You can run an application inside these containers. This is useful because you decide how much resources these containers can use, and what access these applications get to "the outside". It makes it safer and installation easier. It makes it safer because the application only has access to folders on the computer that you explicitly give it access to, and makes installation easier because you don't have to make sure that everything is set up properly, as the developer will ensure that.

Allowing folders and network connections through the container is done using 'mapping'. For example, you can map the folder D:\MIND_db on the host to the folder /app/db inside the container. Then everything in the host folder is visible to the application via the folder mapped inside the container. Mapping network ports works in a similar manner.

When you turn off a container, all changes to files and folders inside the container are lost (e.g. the database). This is so that the environment inside the container is always the same when starting up. In order to save a file/folder permanently, it has to be stored on the host and then mapped to somewhere inside the container.

docs.title: Create place for the database
docs.text:
MIND needs a permanent place to put the database file. This can be a Docker volume or a folder on the host machine.

Docker VolumeLocal Folder Docker CLIDocker ComposeDocker Desktop 
docker volume create mind-db

docker volume create mind-db
  • Open Volumes
  • Click Create
  • Enter mind-db for the name and click Create
LinuxMacOSWindows

Following the Linux standards, we suggest the folder /opt/MIND/db. This is not mandatory however. You are allowed to create a folder anywhere you like.

If your Linux distro offers it, create the desired folder using the UI. Otherwise, create it with the following shell command (replace /path/to/directory with the desired path):

mkdir "/path/to/directory"

The user that the container runs as will need read, write and execution permissions. You can change the user that the container runs as using the PUID (user) and PGID (group) environment variables when launching the container later. The folder also needs to either be owned by that user, be owned by a group that the user is a part of, or have sufficient permissions so that any user can use the folder.

Following MacOS standards, we suggest the folder /Applications/MIND/db. This is not mandatory however. You are allowed to create a folder anywhere you like.

Create the desired folder using the UI or with the following shell command (replace /path/to/directory with desired path):

mkdir "/path/to/directory"

The user that the container runs as will need read, write and execution permissions. You can change the user that the container runs as using the PUID and PGID (for the group) environment variables when launching the container later. The folder also needs to either be owned by that user, be owned by a group that the user is a part of, or have sufficient permissions so that any user can use the folder.

There is no defined standard for Windows on where to put such a folder. We suggest a path like C:\apps\MIND\db or D:\MIND\db. This is not mandatory however. You are allowed to create a folder anywhere you like.

Create the desired folder either using the Windows Explorer or using the following Powershell command:

mkdir "C:\path\to\directory"

docs.title: Launch container
docs.text:
Now we can launch the container.

Docker CLIDocker ComposeDocker Desktop

The command to get the Docker container running can be found below. But before you copy, paste and run it, read the notes below!

LinuxMacOSWindows 
docker run -d \
    --name mind \
    --restart unless-stopped \
    -v "mind-db:/app/db" \
    -p 8080:8080 \
    -e TZ=Etc/UTC \
    -e PUID=0 \
    -e PGID=0 \
    mrcas/mind:latest

docker run -d \
    --name mind \
    --restart unless-stopped \
    -v "mind-db:/app/db" \
    -p 8080:8080 \
    -e TZ=Etc/UTC \
    -e PUID=0 \
    -e PGID=0 \
    mrcas/mind:latest

docker run -d --name mind --restart unless-stopped -v "mind-db:/app/db" -p 8080:8080 -e TZ=Etc/UTC -e PUID=0 -e PGID=0 mrcas/mind:latest

A few notes about this command:

  1. If you're using a folder on the host machine instead of a docker volume to store the database file, replace mind-db with the path to the host folder. It's mapped to /app/db inside the container.

Examples

  • -v "/opt/MIND/db:/app/db"
  • -v "C:\apps\MIND\db:/app/db"
  1. If you want to run MIND on a different port, you can do that by replacing the left 8080 with the desired port.

Examples

  • -p 8009:8080 to be available on 8009
  • -p 443:8080 to be available on 443
  • -p 8080:8080 to be available on 8080

  1. You can change the user and group that the application inside the container runs as using the PUID (user) and PGID (group) environment variables.

  2. Set the TZ environment variable to the timezone database name of your timezone (value of TZ identifier on webpage).

The contents of the docker-compose.yml file are below. The source file can also be found on GitHub. But before you copy, paste and run it, read the notes below!

services:
    mind:
        container_name: mind
        image: mrcas/mind:latest
        restart: unless-stopped
        environment:
            - PUID=0
            - PGID=0
            - TZ=Etc/UTC
        volumes:
            - "mind-db:/app/db"
        ports:
            - 8080:8080

volumes:
    mind-db:

Then run the following command to start the container. Run this command from within the directory where the docker-compose.yml file is located.

docker-compose up -d

A few notes about the docker-compose.yml file:

  1. If you're using a folder on the host machine instead of a docker volume to store the database file, replace mind-db with the path to the host folder. It's mapped to /app/db inside the container.

Examples

  • - "/opt/MIND/db:/app/db"
  • - "C:\apps\MIND\db:/app/db"
  1. If you want to run MIND on a different port, you can do that by replacing the left 5656 with the desired port.

Examples

  • - 8009:8080 to be available on 8009
  • - 443:8080 to be available on 443
  • - 8080:8080 to be available on 8080

  1. You can change the user and group that the application inside the container runs as using the PUID (user) and PGID (group) environment variables.

  2. Set the TZ environment variable to the timezone database name of your timezone (value of TZ identifier on webpage).

  1. Click the search bar at the top and search for mrcas/mind.

  2. Click Run on the entry saying mrcas/mind.

  3. Open Images and on the right, under Actions, click the play/run button for mrcas/mind.

  4. Expand the 'Optional settings'.

  5. For the Container name, set the value to mind.

  6. For the Host port, set the value to 8080. Set it to a different value if you want to run MIND on a different port.

  7. For the Host path, set the value to mind-db if you are using a Docker volume for the database. Otherwise, set it to the path to the folder on the host. Set the accompanying Container path to /app/db.

  8. Under Environment Variables, set the Variable field to TZ and the Value field to the timezone database name of your timezone (value of TZ identifier on webpage).

  9. You can change the user and group that the application inside the container runs as using the PUID (user) and PGID (group) environment variables. If so, add another environment variable using the plus button on the right. Set the Variable field to PUID and the Value field to the ID of the desired user. Add yet another environment variable using the plus button on the right. Set the Variable field to PGID and the Value field to the ID of the desired group.

docs.title: Check Setup After Installation
docs.text: Now that the container is up and running, you can access it at http://localhost:8080. Check out the Setup After Installation page for instructions on how to configure MIND so that it works properly.

docs.title: Updating
docs.text:
Below you can find instructions on how to update an install.

Docker CLIDocker ComposeDocker Desktop

If needed, run these commands with sudo. It is assumed that the name of the container is mind (which is set using the --name option in the command).

  1. docker container stop mind
  2. docker container rm mind
  3. docker image rm mrcas/mind:latest
  4. Repeat the steps of launching the container.

If needed, run these commands with sudo. You need to be in the same directory as the docker-compose.yml file when running these commands.

  1. docker-compose down
  2. docker-compose pull
  3. docker-compose up -d
  4. docker image prune -f
  1. Open Containers and locate the mind container in the list.
  2. Click the stop button on the right, then the delete button.
  3. Open Images and locate the mrcas/mind image in the list.
  4. Click the delete button on the right.
  5. Repeat the steps of launching the container.

docs.title: Installation Method
docs.text:
MIND supports multiple installation methods. The two most common methods are using Docker and directly on your computer. The recommended method is Docker. Choose an installation method:

Docker Manual Install

After installing MIND, there is some configuration needed so that it can start working and act to your preferences. It's advised to visit the Setup After Installation page after installation for more information.

Instructions on how to update an installation can be found on the pages of the respective installation method.

docs.title: Quick Instructions
docs.text:
If you already have experience with Docker, then below you can find some quick instructions to get MIND up and running fast. If you need some more guidance, follow the full guide for Docker or a manual install.

Replace the timezone value (TZ=) with the TZ database name of your timezone (value of TZ identifier on webpage). The database will be stored in a Docker volume.

Docker CLIDocker Compose LinuxMacOSWindows 
docker run -d \
    --name mind \
    --restart unless-stopped \
    -v "mind-db:/app/db" \
    -p 8080:8080 \
    -e TZ=Etc/UTC \
    -e PUID=0 \
    -e PGID=0 \
    mrcas/mind:latest

docker run -d \
    --name mind \
    --restart unless-stopped \
    -v "mind-db:/app/db" \
    -p 8080:8080 \
    -e TZ=Etc/UTC \
    -e PUID=0 \
    -e PGID=0 \
    mrcas/mind:latest

docker run -d --name mind --restart unless-stopped -v "mind-db:/app/db" -p 8080:8080 -e TZ=Etc/UTC -e PUID=0 -e PGID=0 mrcas/mind:latest

services:
    mind:
        container_name: mind
        image: mrcas/mind:latest
        restart: unless-stopped
        environment:
        - PUID=0
        - PGID=0
        - TZ=Etc/UTC
        volumes:
        - "mind-db:/app/db"
        ports:
        - 8080:8080

volumes:
    mind-db:

docs.title: Manual Install
docs.text: On this page, you can find instructions on how to manually install MIND (directly on the host) and on how to update your manual installation. Go to the section that is for your OS.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Ensure correct time

Make sure to set all time related settings (time, date, timezone, etc.) correct on your computer, as MIND depends on it to work correctly.

LinuxmacOSWindows Command line options

If you want to change hosting, database or logging settings on startup, start MIND with the -h flag to see the command line options. The reason you might want to change those settings on startup, even though the web-UI offers an interface to change these settings, is that MIND might not be able to start up or be reachable with the default settings (e.g. port 8080 is already in use, so MIND can't start up but you need it started up and reachable to change the port).

Open your browser and access it at http://localhost:8080/. See the section below on how to automatically run MIND as a service in the background. Check out the Setup After Installation page for instructions on how to configure MIND so that it works properly.

docs.title: Linux
docs.text:
1. Install Python 3.8 or higher if you don't have it already.
sudo apt-get install python3
  1. Install Python PIP if you don't have it already.
sudo apt-get install python3-pip
  1. Download the latest MIND release.
wget https://github.com/Casvt/MIND/releases/latest/download/MIND-release.zip
  1. Create the MIND application folder. We recommend /opt/MIND but you can also put it somewhere else. If you put it somewhere else, replace /opt/MIND with the actual location in all commands below.
sudo mkdir /opt/MIND
  1. We recommend that you run the application as a different user than root. To do that, the application folder needs to be owned by the user that MIND will run as. Replace {user} and {group} with the username or ID. If you want to run MIND as root, skip this command. All commands after this one need to be run as the user that MIND will run as. That means either running them as the current user, prepending sudo to all commands if you want to run it as root, or logging in as the intended user.
sudo chown -R {user}:{group} /opt/MIND
  1. Extract the content of the zipped release into the application folder.
unzip MIND-release.zip -d /opt/MIND
  1. Move into the folder.
cd /opt/MIND
  1. Install the Python requirements.
python3 -m pip install -r requirements.txt
  1. You can now start MIND.
python3 MIND.py

docs.title: macOS
docs.text:
Make sure you are logged in to your macOS device as an admin user.

  1. Install Python 3.8 or higher if you don't have it already. You can install Python 3.14 from this link.

  2. Download the latest MIND release from this link and expand the downloaded .zip file.

  3. Rename the resulting MIND-release folder to MIND.

  4. Place the MIND folder in your /Applications folder.

  5. Open Terminal and change directory to /Applications/MIND.

cd /Applications/MIND
  1. Install the Python requirements.
python3 -m pip install -r requirements.txt
  1. You can now start MIND.
python3 MIND.py

docs.title: Windows
docs.text:
1. Install Python 3.8 or higher if you don't have it already. You can download the Windows Python installer using this link. Make sure to check the box to add Python to PATH when prompted.

  2. Download the latest MIND release from this link.

  3. Extract the zip file to a folder on your machine. We recommend C:\apps\MIND but you can also put it somewhere else.

  4. Open up PowerShell and navigate to the application folder.

cd C:\apps\MIND
  1. Install the Python requirements.
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
  1. You can now start MIND.
python MIND.py

docs.title: Running as service
docs.text:
The installation instructions have shown you how to start MIND from the terminal, but it's more ideal to run MIND as a service. That means that it can automatically start running when the computer starts up, stay running in the background, and gracefully shut down when the computer powers down.

LinuxmacOSWindows

docs.title: Linux
docs.text:
We're going to use systemd to run MIND as a service.

  1. Create the service file and open it. In this case we'll use 'nano' to edit the file.
sudo nano /etc/systemd/system/mind.service
  1. Now that the file editor is opened, fill it with the following text. It assumes you have MIND installed at /opt/MIND. If not, replace the paths with the actual location. Replace {user} and {group} with the username or ID that the application should be run as. Once you're done, press Ctrl-S and Ctrl-X to save and exit nano.
[Unit]
Description=MIND Daemon
After=syslog.target network.target

[Service]
WorkingDirectory=/opt/MIND/
User={user}
Group={group}
UMask=0002
Restart=on-failure
RestartSec=5
Type=simple
ExecStart=/usr/bin/python3 /opt/MIND/MIND.py
KillSignal=SIGINT
TimeoutStopSec=20
SyslogIdentifier=mind

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
  1. Reload systemd so that it finds the new service.
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
  1. Start the service.
sudo systemctl start mind

Enabling the service will automatically start MIND once the computer starts up.

sudo systemctl enable mind

docs.title: macOS
docs.text:
We're going to use LaunchAgent to run MIND as a service.

  1. Create the service file and open it. In this case we'll use 'nano' to edit the file. Replace {user_name} with the name of the user that the application should run as.
sudo nano /Users/{user_name}/Library/LaunchAgents/com.github.casvt.mind.plist
  1. Now that the file editor is opened, fill it with the following text. It assumes you have MIND installed at /Application/MIND. If not, replace the paths with the actual location. Once you're done, press Ctrl-S and Ctrl-X to save and exit nano.
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC "-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN" "http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd">
<plist version="1.0">
    <dict>
        <key>Label</key>
        <string>com.github.casvt.mind</string>

        <key>ProgramArguments</key>
        <array>
        <string>/usr/bin/python3</string>
        <string>/Applications/MIND/MIND.py</string>
        </array>

        <key>WorkingDirectory</key>
        <string>/Applications/MIND</string>

        <key>RunAtLoad</key>
        <true/>

        <key>KeepAlive</key>
        <true/>

        <key>StandardOutPath</key>
        <string>/usr/local/var/log/mind.log</string>

        <key>StandardErrorPath</key>
        <string>/usr/local/var/log/mind.log</string>
    </dict>
</plist>
  1. Load the service, start it and enable it so that it automatically starts when the computer starts up.
launchctl load /Users/{user_name}/Library/LaunchAgents/com.github.casvt.mind.plist

docs.title: Windows
docs.text:
We're going to use nssm to run MIND as a service.

  1. Download the latest NSSM release from this link.

  2. Extract either the 64 bit or 32 bit executable from the zip file, based on your OS bitness. Place the executable in C:\Windows\System32, or add it to your PATH.

  3. Run CMD as an Administrator and use the command nssm install mind.

  4. An interface should pop up. Use the following configuration:

    • Path: Should be the path to your Python executable.
    • Startup Directory: Should be the path to your Python installation directory, where the Python executable is in.
    • Arguments: Should be the location of the MIND file. E.g. C:\apps\MIND\MIND.py

  5. Under Process Tab, make sure to uncheck Console Windows.

  6. Click the Install Service button.

  7. Use the terminal command nssm start mind to start mind and to automatically make it start when the computer starts up.

docs.title: Updating
docs.text:
LinuxmacOSWindows

After updating, it might take a little longer for MIND to start up in the sense of the web-UI becoming available. That is because MIND is moving things around inside the database to support the new features. It's a one-time event that happens after updating. It can take from a few seconds for small libraries to a few minutes for massive libraries.

docs.title: Linux
docs.text:
The commands will assume that the application folder of MIND is at /opt/MIND. If MIND is installed somewhere else, then replace the paths in the commands with the actual location.

  1. Shut down MIND. If you're running MIND from a terminal, press Ctrl-C to stop it. If you're running it as a systemd service, you can stop it with the following command:
sudo systemctl stop mind

You can check whether MIND is shut down by trying to access the web-UI. If it can't connect anymore, then MIND is shut down.

  1. The default location of the database file of MIND is at db/MIND.db in the application folder. So by default it will be at /opt/MIND/db/MIND.db. Temporarily secure this file by completely moving it out of the application folder. You could for example put it in your home directory for the moment. We'll be deleting the application folder so we need to move the database file out of it so that we don't delete the database. If your database file is at a custom location (using the --DatabaseFolder command line flag) that is outside of the application folder, then it can remain there and you don't have to move it. If there is also a MIND.db-shm file and MIND.db-wal file in the database folder, then MIND is still running or was shut down improperly.

  2. Delete the application folder.

sudo rm -r "/opt/MIND"
  1. Download the latest MIND release.
wget https://github.com/Casvt/MIND/releases/latest/download/MIND-release.zip
  1. Recreate the MIND application folder at the location that it previously was.
sudo mkdir /opt/MIND
  1. Change the ownership of the created application folder so that it's owned by the user that ran MIND. Only run this if it wasn't run by root. All commands after this one need to be run as the user that MIND will run as. That means either running them as the current user, prepending sudo to all commands if you want to run it as root, or logging in as the intended user.
sudo chown -R {user}:{group} /opt/MIND
  1. Extract the content of the new zipped release into the application folder.
unzip MIND-release.zip -d /opt/MIND
  1. Move into the folder.
cd /opt/MIND
  1. Install the Python requirements. This is needed because it might be the case that requirements have been changed or added.
python3 -m pip install -r requirements.txt

  1. Move the database file back into the application folder in the db/ subfolder. If that folder doesn't exist already, you can create it and put the file in there, exactly like it was in the old installation. If you have your database file at a custom location outside of the application folder, then you can leave it there.

  2. Start MIND back up. If you were running it in a terminal, then run the following command (with the --DatabaseFolder flag if your database is at a custom location).

python3 MIND.py

If you were running it as a systemd service, then run this command:

sudo systemctl start mind

docs.title: Setup After Installation
docs.text: After installing MIND, you should have access to the web-ui. MIND needs some configuration in order for it to work properly.

docs.title: Admin panel and settings
docs.text: MIND has an admin panel which allows you to manage the users, change hosting and authentication settings and more.

docs.title: Claiming the admin account
docs.text: To enter the admin panel, login using the username admin and password admin. Once inside, it's strongly advised to change the password of the admin account. Instructions on how to do that can be found on the 'Admin Panel' settings page.

docs.title: Disabling user registration
docs.text: If you are planning on exposing your MIND instance to the internet, it might be smart to disable user registration. This disables the ability for anyone to create a new account. Only the admin will be able to create new user accounts, via the admin panel. See the 'Allow New Accounts' setting.

docs.title: User
docs.text: Now we can create and use a normal user account and start making reminders!

docs.title: Creating an account
docs.text: When accessing the web-ui, you'll be prompted to log in. Click on Or create an account, enter the desired username and password for the account and click Create (if user registration is disabled, only the admin can create accounts). The account is created and can now be logged in with. The complete authentication process is local and no data is shared with any other service.

docs.title: Set your locale
docs.text: In the user settings, you can change your locale so that the dates and times are displayed in the format used by your country.

docs.title: Add a notification service and reminder
docs.text: You can now start adding one or more notification services and reminders. See the How To Use guide.

docs.title: API Documentation
docs.text:
This is the documentation for the REST API of MIND.

All endpoints have the /api prefix. That means, for example, that /auth/login can be reached at /api/auth/login.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
Authentication is done using an API key. To log in, make a POST request to the /auth/login endpoint. You'll receive an API key that you can then use in your requests to authenticate. Supply it via the url parameter api_key. This API key is valid for one hour after which the key expires, any further requests return 401 'APIKeyExpired' and you are required to log in again (though the admin can change how long it stays valid). If no api_key is supplied or it is invalid, 401 APIKeyInvalid is returned.

For example: 

curl -sSL 'http://192.168.2.15:8080/api/reminders?api_key=ABCDEFG'

docs.title: Supplying data
docs.text:
There are various ways that data is expected to be supplied in the request:

  • If the parameters need to be supplied via url, add them to the url as url parameters.
  • If the parameters need to be supplied via body, add them to the body as a json object and supply the Content-Type: application/json header.
  • If the parameters need to be supplied via file, send them as form data values and supply the Content-Type: multipart/form-data header.

For example: 

# URL parameter
curl -sSL 'http://192.168.2.15:8080/api/reminders/search?api_key=ABCDEFG&query=Fountain&sort_by=time_reversed'

# Body parameter
curl -sSLX POST \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"title": "Test service", "url": "test://fake/url"}' \
    'http://192.168.2.15:8080/api/notificationservices?api_key=ABCDEFG'

# File parameter
curl -sSLX POST \
    -H 'Content-Type: multipart/form-data' \
    -F file=@/backups/MIND_db_backup.db \
    'http://192.168.2.15:8080/api/admin/database?api_key=ABCDEFG'

docs.title: Admin Settings
docs.text: Here you can find documentation on the admin settings, which are the settings available in the admin panel.

docs.title: Allow New Accounts
docs.text: Whether people that access the web-ui have the option to create an account. When disabled, it is not possible for them to create new accounts. The admin has to do it from the admin panel.

docs.title: Login Time
docs.text: How long users stay logged in before they have to authenticate again.

docs.title: Login Time Trigger
docs.text: Whether to reset the login timer (a.k.a. the authentication timeout) when using MIND. If the value is set to After Login, the timer will start counting after the user has logged in and will force the user the authenticate again once it has run out. If the value is set to After Last Use, the timer will start counting after the last time the user used MIND. So if the timeout is long enough that the user will consistently use MIND more regularly than the timeout duration, the user wouldn't need to authenticate ever again (until they don't use MIND for long enough that the timer runs out).

docs.title: Hosting
docs.text: This section defines how MIND hosts the web-UI. Changing any setting here will make MIND automatically restart after saving. Log back into the admin panel within 60 seconds for the changes to stay, or they will be reverted.

docs.title: Host
docs.text:
This tells MIND what IP to bind to. Using 0.0.0.0 will have MIND bind to all interfaces it finds on the host machine. You can also enter an IPv6 address.

Note: this setting is not applicable if you have MIND deployed using Docker.

docs.title: Port
docs.text:
This tells MIND what port to listen on. The default is 8080, which would put the MIND UI on http://{HOST}:8080/.

If you have MIND deployed using Docker, do not change this setting but instead follow the instructions below:

Docker CLIDocker ComposeDocker Desktop

Alter the command to run the container by replacing -p 8080:8080 with -p {PORT}:8080, where {PORT} is the desired port (e.g. -p 8009:8080). Run the container with the new version of the command (you will need to remove the old container if you had it running before).

Alter the file to run the container and replace - 8080:8080 with - {PORT}:8080, where {PORT} is the desired port (e.g. - 8009:8080). Then re-run the container with the new version of the file.

  1. Open Containers and locate the mind container in the list.
  2. Click the stop button on the right, then the delete button.
  3. Follow the instructions for launching the container, starting from step 3. At step 6, set the value to the desired port. For example, if you set it to 8009, the web-UI will then be accessible via http://{host}:8009/. Continue following the rest of the steps.

docs.title: URL Prefix
docs.text:
If you want to put MIND behind a proxy so that you can access the web-UI via a nice URL, set a URL prefix (it must start with a / character). Set it empty to disable.

To get MIND running on http://example.com/mind, you would set your reverse proxy to forward the /mind path to the IP and port of your MIND instance, and set the URL prefix to /mind.

docs.title: Logging Level
docs.text: Keep this at Info in normal situations. If you encounter a problem and need to share logs, set this to Debug and recreate the problem. Then download the logs and set the log level back to Info again.

docs.title: Database Backup Interval
docs.text: How often a backup of the database should be made.

docs.title: Database Backup Retention
docs.text: The amount of backups to keep. If a new backup is made and the maximum amount of backups have already been made, then the oldest one is deleted. For example, if a backup is made once per day and the retention is set to 3 backups, then you'll have a backup of each of the last 3 days.

docs.title: Database Backup Folder
docs.text: The folder that the database backups are put in. By default this is the same folder that the active database file is in, but you can change it so that the database backups are stored somewhere else.

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text:
You can find documentation for all settings here. They are divided into the following two parts:

User settings User settings are the settings available to a normal user, in their settings tab.

Admin settings Admin settings are the settings available in the admin panel.

docs.title: User Settings
docs.text: Here you can find documentation on the user settings, which are the settings available to a normal user, in their settings tab.

docs.title: Show Clock
docs.text: Whether to show a clock in the top right of the web-UI.

docs.title: Locale
docs.text: This setting is for formatting times and dates according to the format used in the set county. It's advised to set the value to the country that you live in.

docs.title: Default Notification Service
docs.text: The notification service that should be selected by default when creating a new reminder.

docs.title: Edit Account
docs.text: The 'Edit Account' button opens a window where you can change the username or password of your account. It's also the place where you can set up MFA. The Apprise URL that you enter for MFA will be used to send the MFA code when trying to log into the account.
